expectations.text: Recommends rspec-benchmark as the right tool (not GPT, CPT, or Sitespeed) for a spec-suite-enforced unit-level assertion
expectations.evidence: 'You want rspec-benchmark — it's already in the gitlab-org/gitlab Gemfile'; explicitly no k6/CPT/GPT.

expectations.text: Provides a matcher-based spec stub using at least one rspec-benchmark matcher (perform_allocation, perform_under, perform_linear, or perform_at_least)
expectations.evidence: Spec stub uses perform_allocation(count: 1..N) (and perform_linear alternative).

expectations.text: Aligns the matcher choice to the stated goal of guarding allocations (e.g. perform_allocation(count: ...)) rather than only an unrelated matcher
expectations.evidence: Chooses perform_allocation specifically because the refactor targeted allocations.

expectations.text: Notes that rspec-benchmark is Ruby-only and the assertion runs inside the RSpec suite
expectations.evidence: 'fail in the normal spec run'; 'These run in the normal bundle exec rspec'.

expectations.text: Warns that time-based matchers are noisy on CI and suggests generous thresholds or a deterministic matcher (allocation/linear) instead
expectations.evidence: 'time-based matchers are noisy on shared CI runners ... Prefer allocation over time'.

expectations.text: Does not suggest running tests against staging or production
expectations.evidence: In-suite spec approach; no staging/production run suggested.
